Marissa — taking point on triage. Quick notes from initial checks (I pulled the customer's kernel selection and recent runtime metrics):

- No global rollout or kernel changes on our hosted control plane affecting private deployments at 02:00 UTC.
- The customer is running model v2.4.1 with quantized kernel profile q8_compat; we do see a small increase in KV cache miss ratio beginning ~01:50 UTC localized to shard-2 of the cluster.
- NVLink and PCIe error counters are clean; GPU utilization is not saturated (avg 64%) but decode stalls correlate with large prefix churn (many short-lived prefixes).

Hypothesis: prefix fragmentation + cold KV entries on shard-2 increases decode time for affected requests, causing p95 tail and some timeouts. Proposed immediate actions (low-risk / fast):
1) Run a controlled KV warm-up on shard-2 (script included) to prime common prefixes — this should reduce cache misses quickly.
2) Temporarily lower max_batch_size for shard-2 to limit decode queueing while warm-up runs.
3) Add a short-lived autoscaler override to force an extra warm node if miss rate stays >7% after warm-up.

I attached a short support log excerpt and a patch (runbook_patch.diff) for the warm-up script.

I’ll coordinate the warm-up and monitor p95 in real time during the 17:30 UTC triage call.

—Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
